sampling_model.design: Observational sampling from a fixed population law; identification is the primary target.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws \((X_i,A_i,Y_i)\sim P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) with finite \(\mathcal X\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment may depend on \((X,U)\); the candidate full-data law restores conditional ignorability given \((X,U)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed stratum has \(0<p_x<1\); constant-\(U\) boundary laws are retained in the closure, and latent positivity is allowed to vanish only in the all-budget Manski limit.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The cell probabilities \((\lambda_x,p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})\) are empirical-frequency estimable; uniform inference through nonsmooth endpoint and level-set maps remains the stated open question.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For fixed sensitivity parameters, the binary mixtures have unique maximum-likelihood solutions and yield a recalculated average treatment effect.
Quantile balancing gives the sharp ATE interval under the marginal sensitivity model.

For binary or low-level categorical exposure and binary outcome, an exposure-standardization sensitivity function is variation-independent of the observed-data distribution and supports three consistent estimators of marginal causal effects.
General bias formulas specialize to outcome contrasts multiplied by changes in the distribution of a binary confounder.
A sharp joint relative-risk bounding factor applies to an unrestricted unmeasured confounder.
A breakdown frontier is the boundary between assumptions that do and do not support a chosen conclusion.
With no restriction on treatment selection, binary potential-outcome means obey worst-case treatment-response bounds.

body.tldr: For binary treatment, outcome, and one shared latent binary confounder within finitely many observed strata, the paper characterizes the exact ATE interval over the finite-simplex closure of strictly positive laws satisfying two-sided treatment-confounder and treatment-specific outcome-confounder odds budgets.  Closed joint-cell inequalities define the boundary without assigning a boundary odds ratio.  A unique quadratic-mixture root reduces each outcome budget to two analytic branches; the ATE endpoints then optimize the treated-minus-control contrast over the same posterior pair.  Endpoint-attaining closure laws establish sharpness, a fixed-input exact certificate and a separate parametric algebraic-atlas procedure cover the computational layers, a rational witness proves stable strict tightening over separate armwise pairs, and a piecewise-algebraic zero-tipping surface records where the sign conclusion fails.

project_justification.gap: The original binary-confounder analysis recalculates causal means at fixed parameter tuples, whereas contemporary work studies propensity-only, arbitrary-confounder, or exposure-standardized departures from exchangeability.  None of the inspected results optimizes bounded treatment and outcome odds associations while preserving one shared latent posterior pair across both potential-outcome arms and treating the null-cell boundary through the finite-simplex closure.
project_justification.niche: The restriction is scientifically interpretable and algebraically low dimensional, yet it retains compatibility information discarded by separate armwise or arbitrary-\(U\) relaxations.  That combination permits exact endpoints, constructive sharpness, and a multibudget tipping frontier.
project_justification.fill: The iff identified interval is accompanied by a fixed-input exact degeneracy-complete verifier, a separate parametric zero-tipping atlas, a stable strict-gap theorem, point-identification reductions, and the correctly qualified Manski limit.

body.related_work: Rosenbaum and Rubin \cite{RosenbaumRubin1983Sensitivity} provide the fixed-tuple binary-mixture inversion recovered by Theorem 1, but do not optimize a bounded region or formulate its finite-simplex closure.  VanderWeele and Arah \cite{VanderWeeleArah2011Bias} provide the bias-decomposition identity that motivates the arm-mean map.  Ciocănea-Teodorescu, Gabriel, and Sjölander \cite{CiocaneaGabrielSjolander2022Marginal} give a variation-independent exposure-standardization sensitivity function and estimators for binary or low-level categorical exposure and binary outcome.  Their sensitivity parameters encode standardized departures from exchangeability and are distinct from one shared binary \(U\) constrained simultaneously by treatment-\(U\) and arm-specific outcome-\(U\) odds budgets; their results neither supply the common-\(U\) sharp envelope and certificate nor automatically sharpen it.  Ding and VanderWeele \cite{DingVanderWeele2016WithoutAssumptions} derive a sharp relative-risk factor for arbitrary \(U\), sacrificing the common-binary compatibility used here.  Tan \cite{Tan2006MarginalSensitivity}, Yadlowsky et al. \cite{YadlowskyEtAl2022Bounds}, and Dorn and Guo \cite{DornGuo2023QuantileBalancing} restrict latent treatment odds without companion outcome-\(U\) odds budgets; their optimization and attainability arguments inform this paper.  These published procedures and the common-binary-\(U\) class are generally non-nested, so no numerical dominance comparison is asserted unless an observable-law-dependent budget translation is first proved.  The separate-posterior-pair interval used in Theorem 3 is instead an internal outer relaxation obtained by dropping only the shared-pair constraint.  Masten and Poirier \cite{MastenPoirier2020BreakdownFrontier} motivate inference on assumption frontiers, while Fang and Santos \cite{FangSantos2019InferenceDirectional} and Nabi et al. \cite{NabiEtAl2024SemiparametricSensitivity} supply the adjacent inferential tools for the open sampling problem.  Manski \cite{Manski1990TreatmentResponse} is recovered only in the joint infinite-budget limit with vanishing latent positivity.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The worked witness certificate isolates the common lower and upper stationary points, gives exact rational separate-pair extrema, and replaces the floating-point search by rational Sturm data and positive comparison margins.  The remaining technical risks are the fixed-rational-input proof that \(\mathsf{CERT}\) handles every denominator artifact and positive-dimensional stationary continuum outside this worked instance, and the separate parametric-elimination proof for \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\).  Existence of a finite semialgebraic stratification for arbitrary real inputs does not by itself provide rational isolating intervals or an executable symbolic atlas.  This diagnostic is internal and makes no numerical comparison with a published non-nested sensitivity model.
body.honest_scope: The population formulas, endpoint attainment over the closed finite-simplex class, certificate completeness, strict open-set gap, and tipping stratification are all claims to be proved rather than established facts.  For the strictly positive interior class only the endpoint infimum, supremum, and closure of the identified set are asserted unless an endpoint is separately shown interior.  The odds ratio is never assigned a boundary value; only its probability-scale chart objectives are continuously extended.  Sampling inference at branch ties and stationary continua is deliberately exposed as Open-ended Question 1.  The model assumes a single binary confounder and finite categorical \(X\).  The separate-posterior-pair interval is an internal outer relaxation of this model; the Ciocănea-Teodorescu--Gabriel--Sjölander procedure and published arbitrary-\(U\) and marginal sensitivity models are generally non-nested unless an observable-law-dependent translation is established.  Point identification at \(\Gamma_A=1\) or \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\) and the all-budget Manski limit are required sanity reductions.
